fluff.overview: The Gnome was developed by Clan Hell's Horses as the first Clan-manufactured heavy battle armor design. Introduced in 3056, the suit was created in response to growing Inner Sphere battle armor capabilities that threatened Clan supremacy in armored infantry warfare. Classified as a heavy-weight assault platform, the Gnome combined substantial armor protection with jump capability and fixed weaponry, offering a heavier alternative to the ubiquitous Elemental without sacrificing all mobility. Named after the earth spirit of classical mythology in keeping with the Clan tradition for second-generation battlesuits, the Gnome quickly established itself as a cornerstone of Hell's Horses infantry doctrine and saw adoption by multiple Clans.
fluff.capabilities:
The MRR configuration mounts a medium recoilless rifle as its primary ranged weapon, retaining the heavy battle claw and Advanced SRM 2 launcher. A one-shot LRM 2 provides a single long-range volley to supplement the rifle's moderate engagement range. The detachable missile pack from the Upgrade chassis is carried over.

The recoilless rifle offers a balance between the Bearhunter autocannon's raw close-range power and the base model's ER small laser range. The one-shot LRM capability gives troopers a limited ability to engage targets at distances normally beyond a Gnome's reach, though the single-use nature means this option is best reserved for opening salvos or priority targets. The overall package creates a more flexible combatant than either the Bearhunter or Pulse Laser configurations, though it lacks the sustained firepower of either specialist variant.
fluff.deployment: ComStar and Word of Blake Level I units operating the MRR variant used the six-trooper formation to maximize the impact of their opening LRM volleys. Six simultaneous long-range missiles provided a meaningful first salvo before the unit closed to recoilless rifle range.
fluff.history:
By the time of Operation Revival, battle armor development among the Clans had largely stagnated. The standard Elemental suit had proven so effective that few Clans saw reason to pursue alternatives. Clan Hell's Horses, however, had never abandoned their conviction that infantry diversity offered tactical advantages a single universal design could not match. When rumors reached the Clan homeworlds in 3054 that Inner Sphere powers were fielding specialized battle armor of their own, the Horses took particular notice. Reports of the Draconis Combine's Kanazuchi, an assault-weight suit capable of withstanding a direct hit from a Clan ER PPC, posed a direct challenge to Clan supremacy in armored infantry.

Khan Malavai Fletcher ordered his scientists to develop a Clan answer to the growing Inner Sphere threat. Rather than start from scratch, the Horse scientists revisited the Rhino, a heavy prototype from the Golden Century that had been shelved decades earlier due to mechanical reliability problems and the Elemental's dominance. Applying modern technological advances to the old design's framework, including advances in miniaturized armor technology, they produced a suit that was twice as fast as the Kanazuchi and carried heavier weaponry, though with slightly less armor protection. Following the Clan tradition of naming second-generation battlesuits after elemental spirits, the new design was designated the Gnome after the earth spirit of classical mythology.

The Gnome debuted in the spring of 3056, assigned initially to the Hell's Horses Alpha Keshik. Its first combat test came during Alpha's annual sparring exercise against Omega Keshik, and though the engagement was simulated, the Gnome-equipped troopers caused such disruption among Omega's traditional Elemental formations that Khan Fletcher ordered an immediate increase in production. Fletcher himself became an avid operator of the suit, and during the Horses' ill-fated intervention in the Combine-Ghost Bear War, he personally accumulated twenty-nine confirmed kills against both BattleMechs and Elementals while wearing Gnome armor.

The Gnome's introduction triggered a broader shift in Clan battle armor philosophy. Other Clans began experimenting with specialized suit designs of their own, producing the Sylph, Salamander, and Undine in relatively quick succession. The Gnome itself spread beyond the Horses' touman through Trials, finding service with multiple Clans. Though later eclipsed in sheer size by newer assault-weight designs, the Gnome remained a mainstay of Hell's Horses front-line Clusters and proved its durability across multiple conflicts.

Production centered on two facilities: Swedenborg Heavy Industries on Kirchbach and the Horses' research complex on Niles. The Upgrade program, introduced during the Jihad era, produced several reconfigured variants with modular weapon mounts and detachable missile systems, reflecting lessons learned from decades of operational use. A separate long-range modification carrying missile and anti-personnel systems emerged from field experience, expanding the suit's tactical envelope beyond its original close-combat role.
